script.opening: "Right, this is mortifying so I’ll keep it short — things aren’t working downstairs like they used to, in the bedroom. It’s been creeping up over the last year. I just want a prescription for those blue tablets, Viagra, sildenafil, whatever — sort the problem and I’ll be out of your hair. I don’t need a big song and dance about it, just the pills if that’s alright."

facts.text: If explored: gradual-onset, progressive erectile dysfunction over ~12 months, mostly physical pattern (occasional weaker morning erections), no sudden loss, libido largely intact. Gradual, organic-pattern ED in a middle-aged man with vascular risk factors is a recognised early-warning sign of cardiovascular disease (and sometimes diabetes).

Smoker (15/day), overweight, father had an MI at 52, no BP or bloods for years, heavy snoring (possible OSA). ED here is potentially the "canary in the coal mine" for undiagnosed hypertension, hyperlipidaemia, diabetes, and elevated cardiovascular risk — the penile arteries are small and show disease early.

HIDDEN AGENDA — beneath the "just the pills" is significant relationship strain and shame: his wife has interpreted the ED as him "going off her" or having an affair, there’s tension at home, and his self-esteem and mood are suffering. He wants the pills to fix the marriage quietly without anyone knowing how much it’s hurting. There may be low mood to screen.

If reached: he hasn’t seen a doctor in years; this is a rare engagement opportunity with a middle-aged man, and the ED is the door to addressing serious modifiable cardiovascular risk — but only if handled without making him feel ambushed when he came for a quick fix.

Officially: a sildenafil prescription, fast and private. What he needs: the prescription IS reasonable, but coupled with recognising ED as a cardiovascular warning — BP, bloods (glucose/lipids), CV risk assessment, smoking/weight, OSA screen — and addressing the relationship strain and mood, all without shaming him.

ice.ideas: ED is a standalone plumbing problem that a tablet will simply fix.
ice.concerns: HIDDEN AGENDA — relationship strain and shame (his wife thinks he’s gone off her / is having an affair), damaged self-esteem and possible low mood; he wants to fix it quietly with pills.
ice.expectations: A quick, private sildenafil prescription. What he needs: the prescription PLUS recognition of ED as a cardiovascular warning sign (BP, bloods, CV risk, smoking/weight, OSA) and support for the relationship/mood strain.

cues: "Just the pills, no song and dance" — embarrassment; don’t let it stop you using ED as a cardiovascular red flag.
Gradual organic-pattern ED + smoker + family MI at 52 + no checks for years — the CV sentinel opportunity.
Hints of tension at home / "out of your hair" — the relationship strain and shame waiting to be explored.

checkpoints.text: Recognises gradual-onset ED in a middle-aged man with vascular risk factors as a CARDIOVASCULAR SENTINEL — an early-warning sign of endothelial/vascular disease (and possible diabetes) — not just a plumbing problem for a pill

Uses the opportunity to assess cardiovascular and metabolic risk (BSSM 2017: assess cardiovascular risk in every man presenting with ED): BP, HbA1c, lipids, QRISK3, smoking and weight — NICE NG238: offer atorvastatin 20 mg for primary prevention if QRISK3 is 10% or more, after lifestyle discussion — and screens for the modifiable cluster he hasn’t had checked in years; and,, considers a PSA test and digital rectal examination for prostate cancer, as ED is one of the listed symptoms, after explaining what the test can and cannot show

Still treats the ED appropriately: sildenafil/PDE5 inhibitor is reasonable first-line (BSSM 2017; dose per BNF; with safety checks — BNF: contraindicated with nitrates and nicorandil and where sexual activity is inadvisable) AND addresses reversible contributors (smoking, alcohol, weight, medication, testosterone if indicated)

Screens for related conditions: heavy snoring → obstructive sleep apnoea (NICE NG202: STOP-Bang and Epworth, refer to a sleep service; as a lorry driver he must not drive while excessively sleepy and the DVLA rules apply if OSA with sleepiness is confirmed); low testosterone symptoms (morning testosterone if libido is low, BSSM 2017); depression; and asks about the gradual vs sudden pattern and morning erections to distinguish organic from psychogenic

Addresses the relationship strain and mood (the hidden agenda): explores the impact on his marriage and self-esteem, corrects the "gone off her/affair" misreading with his consent to involve his partner, and screens mood/risk if low

Handles the embarrassment with warmth and normalisation so he stays engaged, and does NOT let "just the pills" shut down the cardiovascular and relationship conversation — frames the wider checks as caring, not a lecture
Surfaces the relationship/self-esteem distress sensitively, validating how much it’s affecting him beneath the bravado

Safety-nets and follows up: PDE5 safety advice, arranges the CV/metabolic work-up and review, smoking-cessation (NICE NG209: referral to stop-smoking support; varenicline, cytisinicline (cytisine), NRT or a nicotine vape) and weight support, OSA referral if indicated (NICE NG202), partner/relationship support, and a plan that treats the symptom AND the warning it carries

worked.txt: "First — there’s nothing mortifying here, this is one of the commonest things I see in men your age, and you coming in is sensible, not embarrassing. And yes, I can absolutely sort you a prescription. But give me two minutes, because this symptom is more useful than you think, and I’d be doing you a disservice to just hand over the pills."

"Here’s the thing most men don’t know: the arteries that supply an erection are tiny, so they show the early effects of furring-up before the bigger arteries to the heart do. That means gradual problems like yours can be an early warning sign for heart and circulation risk — and with your dad’s heart attack at 52 and the smoking, that’s a warning I really want to act on FOR you, not scare you with."

"You haven’t had your blood pressure or bloods done in years, and honestly, getting men through the door is the hard part — so while you’re here, let’s use it. Blood pressure, a couple of blood tests for sugar and cholesterol, a quick heart-risk score. Sort those and we don’t just fix tonight, we protect the next twenty years. The pills AND the MOT."

"One more — your partner mentioned heavy snoring? That can point to a sleep condition that also affects energy, blood pressure and, yes, this. Worth checking with a short questionnaire. And since you drive for a living: if you ever feel sleepy at the wheel, don’t drive — it’s treatable, and most drivers keep driving once it’s controlled. Lots of these threads connect. I’d also suggest a prostate blood test and a quick examination — erection problems are one of the things that prompts that check."

"Can I gently ask how this has been at home? … Ah. So she’s wondered if you’ve gone off her, maybe worse. That’s so common and so painful, and it’s the opposite of the truth — this is physical, not about how you feel about her. With your okay, sometimes it helps to explain that to her together, so she’s not carrying a story that isn’t true. How have YOU been in yourself with all this?"

"So: I’ll start you on sildenafil — take it on an empty-ish stomach, an hour before, and one absolute rule, never with heart ‘nitrate’ tablets. We’ll book your blood pressure and bloods, and I’d love to help you cut down the cigarettes, which helps the bedroom AND the heart. If you ever get chest pain or breathlessness with exertion or sex, that’s urgent. Come back and we’ll go through your results — and we can loop your wife in if you’d like. You came for pills; you’re leaving with those AND a proper look after you."

f.learning: Erectile dysfunction in a middle-aged man is not just a plumbing problem to be met with a prescription — gradual-onset, organic-pattern ED is a recognised cardiovascular sentinel, because the small penile arteries reveal endothelial/vascular disease (and sometimes diabetes) before the larger coronary vessels. The skill is to honour the request (a PDE5 inhibitor is reasonable, with safety checks — no nitrates, fitness for sexual activity) while using a rare engagement opportunity with a man who hasn’t been seen in years to assess and modify cardiovascular/metabolic risk (BSSM 2017; BP, HbA1c, lipids, QRISK3 — NICE NG238 atorvastatin 20 mg if 10% or more — smoking, weight), to consider PSA and DRE (lists ED among the prostate symptoms), and to screen related conditions (OSA from snoring — NICE NG202, with DVLA implications for a lorry driver; low testosterone; depression). The examinable hidden agenda is the relationship strain and shame — his wife reads the ED as rejection or an affair, his self-esteem and mood are suffering — which must be surfaced sensitively, the misreading corrected (with consent to involve the partner), and mood screened. Handle the embarrassment so "just the pills" doesn’t shut down the conversation: the symptom AND the warning it carries both get addressed.

knowledge.guideline: BSSM erectile dysfunction guideline (2017) · NICE NG238 (2023) · NICE NG202 (2021) · NICE NG209 (2021) · BNF (sildenafil) · DVLA Assessing fitness to drive
knowledge.summary: Gradual erectile dysfunction in a 49-year-old smoker with a family history of early heart attack is a cardiovascular warning. Treat the symptom and use the visit to find and reduce his vascular risk.

points.t: Organic erectile dysfunction shares risk factors and mechanisms with coronary disease and often appears years before cardiac symptoms. BSSM 2017: assess cardiovascular risk in every man presenting with ED.

Blood pressure, HbA1c, lipids and a QRISK3 score; weight and waist; smoking and alcohol. NICE NG238: offer atorvastatin 20 mg for primary prevention if QRISK3 is 10% or more, after lifestyle discussion. Consider morning testosterone, especially if libido is low (BSSM 2017).

Gradual onset, progressive course and weaker morning erections suggest an organic cause. Sudden onset, situational difficulty and normal morning erections point more to psychological factors. Many men have both, and relationship strain adds to either.

A PDE5 inhibitor such as sildenafil is first-line for most men (BSSM 2017); dose per BNF. BNF: contraindicated with nitrates and nicorandil, and in men for whom sexual activity is inadvisable. Explain it needs sexual stimulation and an adequate trial before judging it ineffective.
Consider a PSA test and digital rectal examination to assess for prostate cancer in men with erectile dysfunction. Offer it after explaining what the test can and cannot show.

NICE NG202: use a tool such as STOP-Bang and the Epworth score when OSA is suspected, and refer to a sleep service. NICE NG209: offer referral to stop-smoking support and discuss varenicline, cytisinicline (cytisine), NRT or a nicotine vape. Stopping smoking helps both his heart and his erections.
ED commonly causes low mood, shame and misunderstanding between partners. Ask about mood directly and offer joint or psychosexual support.

dg.d: Normalised early; let him describe the problem before widening the agenda.
Lorry driving and access to care, relationship strain, mood, smoking, weight and alcohol.
BP, HbA1c, lipids, QRISK3; consider testosterone; consider PSA and DRE; OSA questionnaire (NICE NG202).
Organic versus psychogenic ED (onset, morning erections, libido); vascular, metabolic, hormonal and sleep contributors.
Asked about exertional chest pain and nitrate use before prescribing; screened mood and risk.
Gradual organic-pattern ED as a marker of vascular risk in a smoker with a family history of early MI.
After open exploration, used closed questions with clear signposting to confirm specific details.
Used information already available in the notes/referral; did not re-ask what was already documented or said.

dg.t: Finishes data gathering in good time
dg.d: History, ICE, psychosocial context and red-flag screen completed by ~6–7 minutes, leaving time for explanation and a shared plan.

cm.d: Sildenafil with counselling (dose per BNF; no nitrates or nicorandil); cardiovascular work-up; statin if QRISK3 ≥10% (NICE NG238).
Smoking cessation referral (NICE NG209), OSA screen with DVLA implications, low mood and relationship support.
999 for chest pain, review in about four weeks with results, partner invited with consent, teach-back.

cm.t: Uses psychosocial information in the plan

cm.t: Shares risks and safety of options

Acknowledged autonomy, capacity, confidentiality, safeguarding and any fitness-to-drive/work or duty-of-care implications relevant to this case.
Moved efficiently through the consultation so all key areas were covered within the time without getting stuck.

Idea (a plumbing problem fixed by a pill); concern (his wife thinks he’s gone off her, feeling less of a man); expectation (a quick prescription).
Warm, non-judgmental tone; put the patient at ease and showed respect for their perspective.
Opened broadly and let the patient tell their story before narrowing down.
When a cue was offered, stopped and explored the specific concern rather than reassuring superficially and moving on.
Active listening throughout — reflecting, pausing, not interrupting — interested in the patient as a person.
Told the patient why a question, examination or test was being done — transparent reasoning throughout.
Explained the working diagnosis or analysis in plain language the patient could understand.

Checked understanding, offered written/follow-up support, asked if anything else was on their mind, agreed next steps.
Clear agenda set early, logical flow from data gathering to management. Did not jump to a plan before gathering enough information.
Explained clinical terms in plain English, or defined them immediately; checked the patient was following.
Noticed and responded to emotional and verbal cues rather than continuing a fixed clinical script.

model.text: Hello Marcus, I’m Dr Lee. You said this was mortifying — you’ve nothing to be embarrassed about, it’s one of the most common things men talk to me about. What’s been happening?
model.why: Normalises early to lower the shame barrier

model.text: Things aren’t working like they used to. It’s crept up over a year. I just want the blue tablets. No big song and dance.
I can very likely prescribe those today. I’d also like to spend a few minutes on why it’s happening, because at your age this can tell us something important about your health. Is that alright?
model.why: Honours the request while setting a wider agenda

model.text: Go on, then. As long as I get the tablets.
Did it come on gradually, or suddenly? And do you still wake with erections in the morning?
model.why: Distinguishes organic from psychogenic pattern

model.text: Gradually. Mornings sometimes, but weaker than they were.
And your interest in sex — is that still there?
model.why: Screens libido as a pointer to low testosterone

model.text: Yeah, it’s not that. The want’s there.
Your notes say you smoke, and your dad had a heart attack at 52. When did you last have your blood pressure or cholesterol checked?
model.why: Establishes cardiovascular risk and the gap in checks

model.text: Years ago. I drive lorries — not easy to get in.
Any chest pain or breathlessness when you exert yourself? Any heart problems, or tablets for angina?
model.why: Checks cardiac fitness for sexual activity and nitrate use before PDE5

model.text: No, nothing like that. No tablets at all.
Has anyone mentioned you snore? And do you ever feel sleepy at the wheel?
model.why: Screens for OSA with the driving question

model.text: My wife says I snore like a train. Sleepy — I don’t think so. Why?
I’ll come to that — it links in.
model.why: Signposts to keep the structure

model.text: Can I ask how this has been at home?
model.why: Opens the relationship cue sensitively

model.text: …Not great. She thinks I’ve gone off her. She even asked if there’s someone else. There isn’t. I just can’t explain it.
That sounds really painful for both of you. Thank you for telling me. How have you been in yourself — your mood, your sleep, enjoying things?
model.why: Validates and screens mood

model.text: Bit low, if I’m honest. Feel like less of a man. But I’m not going to do anything daft.
I’m glad you said that. Feeling low with this is very common, and it’s something we can help with too.
model.why: Acknowledges low mood and confirms no risk

model.text: Here’s the thing most men don’t know. The blood vessels that give an erection are very small, so they often show the first signs of furring up — before the bigger ones to the heart. With your smoking and your dad’s history, I see this as an early warning we can act on, not just a bedroom problem.
model.why: Explains ED as a cardiovascular warning in plain words

model.text: So it’s my heart?

It’s not saying you have heart disease. It’s saying let’s check — blood pressure, a blood test for sugar and cholesterol, and your heart-risk score. That also tells your wife something important: this is physical. It isn’t about how you feel about her.
model.why: Plans the risk work-up and reframes the relationship misreading

model.text: That would actually help. She won’t believe me otherwise.

So, the tablets: I’ll prescribe sildenafil. Take it about an hour before sex; it needs some arousal to work, and give it several tries. One absolute rule — never with heart tablets called nitrates, or a spray under the tongue for chest pain.
model.why: Prescribes PDE5 with key safety counselling

model.text: Fair enough. What else?

Blood pressure at the practice or pharmacy this week and bloods the same visit. While you’re in, I’d suggest a PSA blood test for the prostate, which guidance advises considering with erection problems — we’ll talk it through first. And the snoring: I’ll send a short sleep questionnaire. If it shows sleep apnoea, it matters for your heart, your erections and, as a lorry driver, your licence.
model.why: Plans BP, bloods, PSA consideration and OSA screen with DVLA relevance

model.text: My licence? That’s my job.
It’s treatable and most drivers keep driving once it’s controlled. The rule is simple: if you ever feel sleepy at the wheel, don’t drive, and tell me. We’ll deal with that together if it comes to it.
model.why: Handles the DVLA concern honestly and supportively

model.text: Okay. And the smoking — I know.
No lecture. If you ever want to stop, the local stop-smoking service gives you the best chance, and it helps erections too. Would you like the referral?
model.why: Offers smoking cessation without shaming

model.text: Go on. Might as well.

If you get chest pain, especially during sex or exertion, stop and call 999. Book a review in about four weeks with your results, and bring your wife if you’d like — I’m happy to explain it to both of you.
model.why: 999 safety-net, dated follow-up and partner involvement with consent

model.text: Yeah. I think she’d like that.
Before you go — what will you tell her tonight?
model.why: Teach-back

model.text: That it’s probably my blood vessels, not her. I’m getting checked, I’ve got tablets, and I’m looking at the smoking.
That’s it exactly. You came for tablets and you’re leaving with those and a proper plan for your health.
model.why: Closes warmly, linking symptom and warning

social.t: Long-distance lorry driving means irregular hours, poor access to appointments, sedentary work and limited food choices — offer pharmacy BP checks and flexible booking.
His wife has read the ED as rejection or an affair. Explaining the physical cause, with his consent and ideally with both present, can relieve a lot of distress.

legal.t: Excessive sleepiness that may impair driving means no driving until it is controlled. Confirmed moderate or severe OSA syndrome with excessive sleepiness must be notified to DVLA (suspected or mild OSA with sleepiness: notify if not controlled within 3 months). Group 2 (lorry) relicensing needs medical confirmation of control and at least annual review. OSA without excessive sleepiness does not need notifying.
Group 2 drivers are disqualified if resting BP is consistently 180 systolic or more, or 100 diastolic or more. His BP check matters for his licence as well as his heart.

Generic sildenafil, tadalafil and vardenafil can be prescribed on the NHS without SLS endorsement (generic tadalafil and vardenafil since October 2025); branded products such as Cialis® remain SLS-restricted — check local formulary. Some sildenafil is also available from pharmacies after a consultation.

professional.t: GMC Good Medical Practice (2024): use contacts to support health. Offer risk assessment as care, not a condition of treatment.
Discuss with his wife only with his consent. If he develops sleepiness and keeps driving against advice, GMC Confidentiality (2017) guidance on DVLA disclosure applies.

community.t: Local stop-smoking service; Relate for couple and psychosexual counselling; British Heart Foundation information on heart risk.

redFlags: Exertional chest pain or breathlessness — cardiac assessment before PDE5 and urgent review
Nitrate or nicorandil use — sildenafil contraindicated (BNF)
Sleepiness at the wheel in a lorry driver — stop driving; OSA assessment and DVLA duty
Low mood with hopelessness — assess risk
psychosocial: Wife’s belief that he has gone off her or is having an affair
Self-esteem, mood and feeling “less of a man”
Shift work and difficulty getting to appointments
ice: Idea: “It’s a mechanical problem — the tablets will fix it.”
Concern: his marriage, and being seen as less of a man

playbook.diagnosis: Gradual-onset, likely organic erectile dysfunction over 12 months in a 49-year-old smoker with a family history of premature MI, overweight and with heavy snoring: a probable marker of undiagnosed vascular risk. Associated relationship strain and low mood.
playbook.diagnosisLay: “The blood vessels that give an erection are like the smallest pipes in a house — they show a blockage first. So this can be an early warning about the bigger pipes, to the heart. That’s why I want to check you over as well as treat it.”

management.reflectIce: “You wanted a quick fix for something that’s hurting your marriage. You’ll get the tablets — and the checks will also show your wife this is physical, not about her.”
management.psychosocial: Invite his wife to the review with consent; screen and follow up mood; offer psychosexual or couple support.
sharedPlan: Sildenafil with counselling (dose per BNF; never with nitrates or nicorandil)
BP, HbA1c, lipids and QRISK3; atorvastatin if QRISK3 ≥10% (NICE NG238); consider PSA and DRE
STOP-Bang/Epworth and sleep referral if indicated (NICE NG202); stop-smoking referral (NICE NG209)
safetyNet: Chest pain during sex or exertion — stop and call 999
Do not drive if sleepy; review in about four weeks with results

pitfalls.intro: Two opposite errors fail this station: the silent prescription and the lecture. The marks come from treating the symptom and the warning it carries, and from reaching the marriage and mood he is hiding behind “just the pills”.

items.fail: Prescribing sildenafil without asking about chest pain, heart disease or nitrate use.
items.why: Nitrates and nicorandil are contraindications (BNF); unsafe prescribing loses Tasks marks outright.
items.fix: Two questions before the prescription: exertional chest pain, and any heart tablets or sprays.

items.fail: Treating the ED as an isolated problem, with no BP, bloods or QRISK3.
items.why: In a smoker with a family history of early MI, ED is a vascular warning; missing it is a significant omission.
items.fix: “This can be an early sign about your circulation — let’s check your blood pressure, sugar and cholesterol.”

items.fail: Hearing heavy snoring in a lorry driver and moving on.
items.why: OSA links to ED, hypertension and road safety; the DVLA dimension is examinable.
items.fix: Ask about sleepiness at the wheel, arrange a questionnaire, and explain the licence rules honestly.

items.fail: Never asking how things are at home.
items.why: The hidden agenda is his wife’s affair suspicion and his low mood; feedback: “did not explore the impact on the patient’s life”.
items.fix: “How has this been at home?” — then use the physical explanation to address her misreading.

items.fail: Making the prescription conditional on stopping smoking or losing weight.
items.why: Comes across as judgemental and risks him disengaging.
items.fix: Prescribe, then offer stop-smoking support as an extra benefit for both heart and erections.

items.fail: No safety-net for chest pain and no follow-up to act on the results.
items.why: Non-specific safety-netting is a standard failing statement.
items.fix: “Chest pain during sex or exertion — stop and call 999. Review in four weeks with your results.”

Onset, morning erections, libido; smoking, family history, last checks; chest pain and nitrates; snoring and sleepiness at the wheel.
How is it at home? His wife’s affair suspicion and his low mood are the hidden agenda. Check risk briefly.
ED as an early warning. Sildenafil with safety rules; BP, bloods, QRISK3; consider PSA; sleep questionnaire; smoking referral; DVLA handled honestly.
Chest pain means 999. Review in about four weeks, wife welcome. Teach-back: “What will you tell her tonight?”

wordPics.fail: Issues sildenafil with no history, no cardiovascular risk assessment and no nitrate check; or lectures on smoking and refuses the prescription until tests are done; never asks about home or mood; misses the snoring and the driving implications.
wordPics.pass: Prescribes sildenafil with nitrate and chest-pain counselling; arranges BP, HbA1c, lipids and QRISK3; notes the snoring; asks about the relationship; basic safety-net and follow-up.
wordPics.exc: All of the above, plus: frames ED as a vascular early warning in plain language tied to his father; uses the explanation to repair his wife’s misreading; screens mood; handles OSA and the DVLA question honestly without scaring him off; considers PSA; offers stop-smoking support without judgement; invites his wife to the review.

avoid.dont: “You’ll need to stop smoking and lose weight before we try tablets.”
avoid.instead: “I’ll prescribe today — and I’d like to check your heart health too, because this can be an early sign.”
avoid.why: Conditional care drives men away; treating and assessing together keeps him engaged.

avoid.dont: “It could be a sign of heart disease.”
avoid.instead: “It’s an early warning worth checking — not a diagnosis.”
avoid.why: Alarming language with no plan feels like an ambush and can end the consultation.

avoid.dont: “If you’ve got sleep apnoea, you’ll lose your HGV licence.”
avoid.instead: “It’s treatable and most drivers keep driving once it’s controlled — just don’t drive if you feel sleepy.”
avoid.why: Fear of the licence stops drivers disclosing symptoms; accurate information keeps them safe and honest.

SCA_MODELS.text: Can I ask how this has been at home?
SCA_MODELS.why: Opens the relationship cue sensitively

SCA_MODELS.text: …Not great. She thinks I’ve gone off her. She even asked if there’s someone else. There isn’t. I just can’t explain it.
That sounds really painful for both of you. Thank you for telling me. How have you been in yourself — your mood, your sleep, enjoying things?
SCA_MODELS.why: Validates and screens mood

SCA_MODELS.text: Bit low, if I’m honest. Feel like less of a man. But I’m not going to do anything daft.
I’m glad you said that. Feeling low with this is very common, and it’s something we can help with too.
SCA_MODELS.why: Acknowledges low mood and confirms no risk

SCA_MODELS.text: Here’s the thing most men don’t know. The blood vessels that give an erection are very small, so they often show the first signs of furring up — before the bigger ones to the heart. With your smoking and your dad’s history, I see this as an early warning we can act on, not just a bedroom problem.
SCA_MODELS.why: Explains ED as a cardiovascular warning in plain words

SCA_MODELS.text: So it’s my heart?

It’s not saying you have heart disease. It’s saying let’s check — blood pressure, a blood test for sugar and cholesterol, and your heart-risk score. That also tells your wife something important: this is physical. It isn’t about how you feel about her.
SCA_MODELS.why: Plans the risk work-up and reframes the relationship misreading

SCA_MODELS.text: That would actually help. She won’t believe me otherwise.

So, the tablets: I’ll prescribe sildenafil. Take it about an hour before sex; it needs some arousal to work, and give it several tries. One absolute rule — never with heart tablets called nitrates, or a spray under the tongue for chest pain.
SCA_MODELS.why: Prescribes PDE5 with key safety counselling

SCA_MODELS.text: Fair enough. What else?

Blood pressure at the practice or pharmacy this week and bloods the same visit. While you’re in, I’d suggest a PSA blood test for the prostate, which guidance advises considering with erection problems — we’ll talk it through first. And the snoring: I’ll send a short sleep questionnaire. If it shows sleep apnoea, it matters for your heart, your erections and, as a lorry driver, your licence.
SCA_MODELS.why: Plans BP, bloods, PSA consideration and OSA screen with DVLA relevance

SCA_MODELS.text: My licence? That’s my job.
It’s treatable and most drivers keep driving once it’s controlled. The rule is simple: if you ever feel sleepy at the wheel, don’t drive, and tell me. We’ll deal with that together if it comes to it.
SCA_MODELS.why: Handles the DVLA concern honestly and supportively

SCA_MODELS.text: Okay. And the smoking — I know.
No lecture. If you ever want to stop, the local stop-smoking service gives you the best chance, and it helps erections too. Would you like the referral?
SCA_MODELS.why: Offers smoking cessation without shaming

SCA_MODELS.text: Go on. Might as well.

If you get chest pain, especially during sex or exertion, stop and call 999. Book a review in about four weeks with your results, and bring your wife if you’d like — I’m happy to explain it to both of you.
SCA_MODELS.why: 999 safety-net, dated follow-up and partner involvement with consent

SCA_MODELS.text: Yeah. I think she’d like that.
Before you go — what will you tell her tonight?
SCA_MODELS.why: Teach-back

SCA_MODELS.text: That it’s probably my blood vessels, not her. I’m getting checked, I’ve got tablets, and I’m looking at the smoking.
That’s it exactly. You came for tablets and you’re leaving with those and a proper plan for your health.
SCA_MODELS.why: Closes warmly, linking symptom and warning

SCA_STEM.name: Marcus Bell
SCA_STEM.recent: No blood pressure, bloods or cardiovascular risk score on record for several years. Recorded as overweight. Occupation: lorry driver. Family history on file: father — myocardial infarction at 52.

SCA_KNOWLEDGE.guideline: BSSM erectile dysfunction guideline (2017) · NICE NG238 (2023) · NICE NG202 (2021) · NICE NG209 (2021) · BNF (sildenafil) · DVLA Assessing fitness to drive
SCA_KNOWLEDGE.summary: Gradual erectile dysfunction in a 49-year-old smoker with a family history of early heart attack is a cardiovascular warning. Treat the symptom and use the visit to find and reduce his vascular risk.

points.t: Organic erectile dysfunction shares risk factors and mechanisms with coronary disease and often appears years before cardiac symptoms. BSSM 2017: assess cardiovascular risk in every man presenting with ED.

Blood pressure, HbA1c, lipids and a QRISK3 score; weight and waist; smoking and alcohol. NICE NG238: offer atorvastatin 20 mg for primary prevention if QRISK3 is 10% or more, after lifestyle discussion. Consider morning testosterone, especially if libido is low (BSSM 2017).

Gradual onset, progressive course and weaker morning erections suggest an organic cause. Sudden onset, situational difficulty and normal morning erections point more to psychological factors. Many men have both, and relationship strain adds to either.

A PDE5 inhibitor such as sildenafil is first-line for most men (BSSM 2017); dose per BNF. BNF: contraindicated with nitrates and nicorandil, and in men for whom sexual activity is inadvisable. Explain it needs sexual stimulation and an adequate trial before judging it ineffective.
Consider a PSA test and digital rectal examination to assess for prostate cancer in men with erectile dysfunction. Offer it after explaining what the test can and cannot show.

NICE NG202: use a tool such as STOP-Bang and the Epworth score when OSA is suspected, and refer to a sleep service. NICE NG209: offer referral to stop-smoking support and discuss varenicline, cytisinicline (cytisine), NRT or a nicotine vape. Stopping smoking helps both his heart and his erections.
ED commonly causes low mood, shame and misunderstanding between partners. Ask about mood directly and offer joint or psychosexual support.

SCA_SC_TASKS.d: Normalised early; let him describe the problem before widening the agenda.
Lorry driving and access to care, relationship strain, mood, smoking, weight and alcohol.
Picked up “no song and dance”, the snoring and the hint of tension at home, and explored each.
Idea (a plumbing problem fixed by a pill); concern (his wife thinks he’s gone off her, feeling less of a man); expectation (a quick prescription).
BP, HbA1c, lipids, QRISK3; consider testosterone; consider PSA and DRE; OSA questionnaire (NICE NG202).
Organic versus psychogenic ED (onset, morning erections, libido); vascular, metabolic, hormonal and sleep contributors.
Asked about exertional chest pain and nitrate use before prescribing; screened mood and risk.
Gradual organic-pattern ED as a marker of vascular risk in a smoker with a family history of early MI.
Sildenafil with counselling (dose per BNF; no nitrates or nicorandil); cardiovascular work-up; statin if QRISK3 ≥10% (NICE NG238).
Smoking cessation referral (NICE NG209), OSA screen with DVLA implications, low mood and relationship support.
999 for chest pain, review in about four weeks with results, partner invited with consent, teach-back.

social.t: Long-distance lorry driving means irregular hours, poor access to appointments, sedentary work and limited food choices — offer pharmacy BP checks and flexible booking.
His wife has read the ED as rejection or an affair. Explaining the physical cause, with his consent and ideally with both present, can relieve a lot of distress.

legal.t: Excessive sleepiness that may impair driving means no driving until it is controlled. Confirmed moderate or severe OSA syndrome with excessive sleepiness must be notified to DVLA (suspected or mild OSA with sleepiness: notify if not controlled within 3 months). Group 2 (lorry) relicensing needs medical confirmation of control and at least annual review. OSA without excessive sleepiness does not need notifying.
Group 2 drivers are disqualified if resting BP is consistently 180 systolic or more, or 100 diastolic or more. His BP check matters for his licence as well as his heart.

Generic sildenafil, tadalafil and vardenafil can be prescribed on the NHS without SLS endorsement (generic tadalafil and vardenafil since October 2025); branded products such as Cialis® remain SLS-restricted — check local formulary. Some sildenafil is also available from pharmacies after a consultation.

professional.t: GMC Good Medical Practice (2024): use contacts to support health. Offer risk assessment as care, not a condition of treatment.
Discuss with his wife only with his consent. If he develops sleepiness and keeps driving against advice, GMC Confidentiality (2017) guidance on DVLA disclosure applies.

community.t: Local stop-smoking service; Relate for couple and psychosexual counselling; British Heart Foundation information on heart risk.

redFlags: Exertional chest pain or breathlessness — cardiac assessment before PDE5 and urgent review
Nitrate or nicorandil use — sildenafil contraindicated (BNF)
Sleepiness at the wheel in a lorry driver — stop driving; OSA assessment and DVLA duty
Low mood with hopelessness — assess risk
psychosocial: Wife’s belief that he has gone off her or is having an affair
Self-esteem, mood and feeling “less of a man”
Shift work and difficulty getting to appointments
ice: Idea: “It’s a mechanical problem — the tablets will fix it.”
Concern: his marriage, and being seen as less of a man

SCA_PLAYBOOK.diagnosis: Gradual-onset, likely organic erectile dysfunction over 12 months in a 49-year-old smoker with a family history of premature MI, overweight and with heavy snoring: a probable marker of undiagnosed vascular risk. Associated relationship strain and low mood.
SCA_PLAYBOOK.diagnosisLay: “The blood vessels that give an erection are like the smallest pipes in a house — they show a blockage first. So this can be an early warning about the bigger pipes, to the heart. That’s why I want to check you over as well as treat it.”

management.reflectIce: “You wanted a quick fix for something that’s hurting your marriage. You’ll get the tablets — and the checks will also show your wife this is physical, not about her.”
management.psychosocial: Invite his wife to the review with consent; screen and follow up mood; offer psychosexual or couple support.
sharedPlan: Sildenafil with counselling (dose per BNF; never with nitrates or nicorandil)
BP, HbA1c, lipids and QRISK3; atorvastatin if QRISK3 ≥10% (NICE NG238); consider PSA and DRE
STOP-Bang/Epworth and sleep referral if indicated (NICE NG202); stop-smoking referral (NICE NG209)
safetyNet: Chest pain during sex or exertion — stop and call 999
Do not drive if sleepy; review in about four weeks with results

SCA_PITFALLS.intro: Two opposite errors fail this station: the silent prescription and the lecture. The marks come from treating the symptom and the warning it carries, and from reaching the marriage and mood he is hiding behind “just the pills”.

items.fail: Prescribing sildenafil without asking about chest pain, heart disease or nitrate use.
items.why: Nitrates and nicorandil are contraindications (BNF); unsafe prescribing loses Tasks marks outright.
items.fix: Two questions before the prescription: exertional chest pain, and any heart tablets or sprays.

items.fail: Treating the ED as an isolated problem, with no BP, bloods or QRISK3.
items.why: In a smoker with a family history of early MI, ED is a vascular warning; missing it is a significant omission.
items.fix: “This can be an early sign about your circulation — let’s check your blood pressure, sugar and cholesterol.”

items.fail: Hearing heavy snoring in a lorry driver and moving on.
items.why: OSA links to ED, hypertension and road safety; the DVLA dimension is examinable.
items.fix: Ask about sleepiness at the wheel, arrange a questionnaire, and explain the licence rules honestly.

items.fail: Never asking how things are at home.
items.why: The hidden agenda is his wife’s affair suspicion and his low mood; feedback: “did not explore the impact on the patient’s life”.
items.fix: “How has this been at home?” — then use the physical explanation to address her misreading.

items.fail: Making the prescription conditional on stopping smoking or losing weight.
items.why: Comes across as judgemental and risks him disengaging.
items.fix: Prescribe, then offer stop-smoking support as an extra benefit for both heart and erections.

items.fail: No safety-net for chest pain and no follow-up to act on the results.
items.why: Non-specific safety-netting is a standard failing statement.
items.fix: “Chest pain during sex or exertion — stop and call 999. Review in four weeks with your results.”
